did_you_know.text: Did you know? The LORD commands Hosea to love an unfaithful woman, thereby portraying the LORD’s love for the Israelites even though they turn to other gods.
Did you know? The verse also describes the Israelites as loving “raisin cakes”—a phrase associated with a drink made from grapes—alongside their turning to other gods.
Did you know? Hosea says that he bought the woman for fifteen pieces of silver, a homer of barley, and a lethek of barley.
Did you know? The verse gives the amounts and goods involved in the transaction, but does not explain their exact value or how they would convert into modern measurements.
Did you know? After buying her, Hosea commands the woman to remain with him for many days, not to prostitute herself or belong to another man.
Did you know? Hosea also makes a commitment of his own: “And I will be the same toward you”—wording that emphasizes a binding relationship and a long period of waiting.
Did you know? The woman’s period of waiting serves as a picture of the time when the Israelites will be without a king or prince—that is, without political leadership.
Did you know? The verse lists several things the Israelites will lack during that period: sacrifice, a sacred pillar, an ephod, and household idols, along with the absence of a king and a prince.
Did you know? According to the chapter’s vision, after that period the Israelites will return, seek the LORD their God and David their king, and stand in awe before the LORD and his goodness.
Did you know? The chapter concludes its vision with the phrase “in the latter days,” referring to the time when the Israelites will return and seek the LORD.
